text:
The Rangers' season changed in October, when Igor Shesterkin went down with a lower-body injury in Washington and the team announced he would miss the rest of the year. Since then the net has belonged to Dylan Garand and Joonas Korpisalo, and the surprising part is how well it has gone: the goaltending has allowed 4.6 fewer goals than the shots deserved. The New York Post called them an "unexpected dynamic goalie tandem" in a Nov 18 headline.

The problem is at the other end. New York has scored 8.4 fewer goals than its chances usually produce, which is the gap between 13-9-1 and something better. The process is fine: 53.4% of the expected goals overall, 55% over the last ten games (6-4-0). Our simulations give them a 67% chance at the playoffs and a projected 95 points, though the division is nearly gone at 1%, with Carolina pulling away.

The lines tell the finishing story. J.T. Miller, Pavel Dorofeyev and Tye Kartye have taken 64% of the expected goals together and been outscored 4-7, the kind of number that tends to flip. Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault are the top line at 55% of the chances but under 50% of the shot attempts.

The three-game winning streak ended with a 5-2 loss to Carolina on Nov 22, outshot 41-27. What to watch: whether the goals start matching the chances before the goaltending comes back to earth.
